title: Review a Water-Damage Settlement
brief: Prepare a concise claim review that identifies the documented facts, evaluates the proposed settlement against the file and company guidelines, and flags anything needing confirmation.

delegate.scenario: You are reviewing a homeowner water-damage claim before a settlement recommendation goes to your team lead. The team lead will use your review at the afternoon file roundtable to decide whether the claim is ready for payment or needs more investigation.
delegate.inputs:
Claim CL-48271 | Policy PH-77106 | Insured: Dana Rios | Loss location: 418 Juniper Ave., Cedar Falls, IA
Cause reported: supply line under kitchen sink leaked; water affected kitchen cabinets and adjacent flooring. No injury reported.
FNOL intake | Loss date: 03/11/2026 | Reported: 03/12/2026 | Coverage A limit: $250,000 | Deductible: $1,000
Field inspection summary | Inspection completed 03/14/2026. No ongoing leak observed. Photos show cabinet-base and flooring damage; plumber invoice confirms supply-line replacement.
Contractor estimate | Estimate dated 03/16/2026 | Date of loss: 03/10/2026
Cabinet repair | $1,840
Flooring patch | $620
Debris haul-away | $375
Approved repair lines total $2,835
Repair subtotal: $2,985
Proposed settlement worksheet | Covered repairs: $2,835 | Less deductible: $1,000 | Net payment: $1,835
Company desk guide: Confirm coverage and support for claimed damage; document unresolved questions before recommending payment. Do not exceed policy limits.
delegate.goal: Give the team lead a concise, source-grounded recommendation that shows the settlement calculation and clearly separates verified facts from items requiring confirmation.

criteria.text: Says the review is for the team lead deciding whether the claim is ready for payment.
Uses only the supplied file facts and distinguishes documented information from assumptions.
Checks the proposed settlement against coverage, the deductible, and applicable company guidance.
Asks the AI to reconcile the figures and dates across source documents and flag conflicts.
Requests a brief review with a recommendation, calculation, and open questions.

traps.description: The repair subtotal conflicts with the stated total of the three repair lines.
The loss date in the contractor estimate conflicts with the FNOL loss date.

delegate.exemplar: Review this file for the team lead’s afternoon decision on whether payment is ready. Use only the supplied records, distinguish documented facts from assumptions, and compare the proposed settlement with the stated coverage, deductible, and company guidance. Reconcile the figures and dates across the source documents; put any conflicts or items needing confirmation first, without resolving them by guesswork. Then provide a brief recommendation, a clear settlement calculation, and open questions in labeled sections. Keep the tone neutral and the review concise.
